text:
alex: seeing a spike in request p95 for inference-hosts in us-west1, started ~3m ago. errorRate on preemptible pools jumped. anyone else?

mira: yep noticed it too, dashboards show a cluster-level eviction burst around 1820004400. some pods restarted.

samir: digging into node termination logs now. GCP returned `SCHEDULED_PREEMPTION` for ~24 GPUs in preemptible-pool-a.

jen: traffic to the hosted endpoint hit 2.2x normal for a few minutes, autoscaler tried to replace but warming caused extra latency.

kai: can we temporarily route traffic to on-demand pool? we have spare capacity in dedicated-USW but need to flip routing.

alex: proposing: 1) pause spot autoscaling 2) increase dedicated pool by 25% 3) add short-term routing weight shift to on-demand. cost vs latency tradeoff. :warning:

mira: +1. how fast can we change weights? routing config is in `infra-config/routing.yaml` with rollout through `infractl`.

samir: I can run the change. command: `infractl rollout routing --region us-west1 --set-weight spot=0.6,dedicated=0.4 --timeout 2m`

alex: let's move to dedicated=0.6 for now and spot=0.4. safer to drop spot weight.

jen: note: function-calling workloads are sensitive to cold starts on dedicated if instances need model warmup. we should preferentially shift shorter requests first.

kai: can we enable prefix KV cache warmup on a subset of nodes to reduce cold latency? runtime team could prime caches. @mira can you coordinate with eng-runtime?

mira: pinging eng-runtime in #eng-runtime: "runtime, we need a small cache warmup for us-west1 dedicated nodes, can you kick off priming for the top 50 Prompts?"

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-345 us-west1 preemptible eviction wave — severity: p2. Assigned: samir.

samir: running the routing rollout now: `infractl rollout routing --region us-west1 --set-weight spot=0.4,dedicated=0.6`

k8s-autoscaler: Alert: node group preemptible-pool-a scaled -18 -> 0 instances in 90s due to repeated evictions.

alex: thanks. after rollout, monitor p95 and error rate for 10m. if not improving, shift to dedicated=0.8.

jen: also toggled `warm-up=true` on dedicated launch-template (small change) to reduce model load delay. doing canary on 2 instances.

mira: confirmed priming job started, ETA ~2m.

samir: routing rollout applied, p95 dropping from 720ms -> 210ms baseline looks better but error spikes still present on specific shards. investigating pod-level OOMs possibly from model cache pressure.

kai: if OOMs are due to mixed-gpu memory fragmentation, we might need to set `runtime.kv_cache.max_entries=80k` on affected nodes. that's a config push.

alex: ok let's hold further traffic shifts until OOMs fixed. samir, can you cordon problematic nodes and drain safely? add label `evicted=true` so autoscaler won't put workloads back there.

samir: cordoning nodes now and adding label. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 && kubectl label node gpu-node-23 evicted=true`

mira: also opening a short-term exception to keep spot autoscaling paused for 20m to let the system stabilize.

jen: monitoring logs for cold-start tail latency. so far so good, warm-up worked on canary.

oncall-bot: Update: Incident INC-2026-345 status -> mitigating. Next update in 10m.

alex: post-mortem action items: 1) add automatic fallback policy when >15% of preemptible pool is lost 2) pre-warm dedicated pool when routing weight change >20% 3) improve eviction alerting to include GPU count.

mira: adding those to the infra backlog. rough estimates: item 1 ~2d, item 2 ~1d, item 3 ~3h.

samir: closing loop — current p95 stable at 230ms, error rate back to baseline. keeping incident open for monitoring until the end of the hour.

alex: huge thanks everyone. cost note: we'll consume ~27% more on-demand for the hour — finance FYI. :memo:
